threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local Word-document processing engine providing Rust byte APIs, a native CLI, PyO3/Python interfaces, WASM interfaces, an npm CLI, and a stdio MCP server. Document packages, XML, legacy DOC data, embedded media, Markdown and edit plans cross into parsers and transformations; results return as bytes or are published to host files. The MCP adapter grants a persistent directory capability for explicit document reads and output publication. Native rendering additionally consumes ambient font resources and maintains a font index. Optional self-update and maintainer publication workflows introduce separate network, executable replacement and registry authority. Sources: src/lib.rs:7-35, src/lib.rs:163-165, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21, src/update.rs:186-210. Architecture reflects inspected HEAD 4e10eca69c42211651ca907f38b74b6d19e6928c; architecture mapping is not completed audit coverage.

Host CPU/memory availability and browser WASM heaps; general and comparison admission budgets differ. src/admission.rs:63-99; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:80-96; SECURITY.md:71-74.

findings.title: Processing renamed XML parts bypasses depth admission and can abort the host
findings.summary: A document author can give an internal XML part a non-.xml/.rels filename and link it as a header/footer, style, footnote/endnote or chart. Admission skips its XML policy, but rendering or comparison recursively parses it and can exhaust the host stack.

severity.rationale: Attacker-supplied document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering host with a small input; no remote service exposure is assumed. Process CPU/memory limits do not prevent a per-process stack-overflow abort.
severity.changeConditions: Isolated disposable conversion processes reduce the application-level impact; a shared conversion service would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source trace establishes the filename-only gate, main-only fallback, relationship-selected bytes and unbounded recursive parser. No runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Caller-controlled package reaches layout
codeEvidence.explanation: `docx_to_pdf` and PNG/report paths share `with_layout`; the package is admitted and opened before header processing.

codeEvidence.label: Admission chooses policy by suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: The inflated part receives XML policy checks only when its name ends in .xml or .rels. An internal header.bin is counted in byte budgets but skipped by XML policy.

codeEvidence.label: Only the main document gets a second check
codeEvidence.explanation: The explicit fallback protects a renamed main part; it does not validate other relationship-selected XML consumers.

codeEvidence.label: Header reference selected from the document
codeEvidence.explanation: An attacker-controlled section reference selects a relationship ID passed to `load_chrome_part`.

codeEvidence.label: Arbitrary internal target read as XML
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected target bytes are decoded as UTF-8 and forwarded to `chrome_part_xml` without a policy check.

codeEvidence.label: Header/footer raw parser
codeEvidence.explanation: `chrome_part_xml` directly invokes the recursive infallible DOM parser on bytes skipped by the admission XML checks.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship controls target path
codeEvidence.explanation: The document relationship ID selects the package target without a filename-extension or content-type restriction.

codeEvidence.label: DOM nesting consumes call stack
codeEvidence.explanation: Each nested element recurses into `parse_element`; this path has no depth budget, so sufficiently deep XML exhausts the host stack.

codeEvidence.label: Comparison admits package bytes
codeEvidence.explanation: The modified input crosses admission before package processing.

codeEvidence.label: Comparison enters preprocessing
codeEvidence.explanation: Distinct admitted packages reach pre_process_markup, which loads relationship-selected auxiliary parts.

codeEvidence.label: Notes targets bypass suffix assumptions
codeEvidence.explanation: Internal footnotes/endnotes relationship targets are read and directly parsed regardless of filename.

codeEvidence.label: Styles target bypasses suffix assumptions
codeEvidence.explanation: The stylesheet selected by its relationship is passed to the raw parser without a per-part check.

codeEvidence.label: Charts bypass suffix assumptions
codeEvidence.explanation: Each internal chart target is selected by relationship type and its bytes enter raw DOM parsing irrespective of filename.

rootCause.summary: The policy gate classifies XML by archive filename, then checks only a renamed main document as a special case. Rendering instead selects header/footer parts by relationships and interprets their bytes as XML regardless of name. The downstream raw DOM parser relies on prior admission and recurses once per element, leaving renamed story parts outside the depth invariant. Comparison preprocessing repeats this boundary mismatch for relationship-selected styles, notes and charts.

findings.remediation: Enforce the active XML policy before parsing every XML relationship target irrespective of extension, or enumerate typed XML parts during admission. Make the raw DOM parser iterative or depth-bounded as defense in depth.

counterEvidence: Normal .xml/.rels parts receive XML checks, and renamed main documents are explicitly rechecked.
Raw parse_xdocument is documented as unchecked; the defect is its use behind a supposedly admitted package boundary, not the existence of that API.
External relationships are not needed; this exploit uses internal package bytes.
limitations: No application code or malicious input was executed; exact crash depth depends on platform and stack size.
validation.summary: Confirmed that a valid minimal main document and its shallow .rels can select a header.bin payload; default archive and byte budgets still allow many thousands of short nested tags. Strict-to-transitional conversion preserves non-XML parts (src/strict_translation.rs:809-831), and PartFs::open bounds bytes rather than applying XML depth (src/opc/mod.rs:282-350). The raw header parser therefore receives the unbounded nesting. Parent source review also confirms the same root gap in comparison preprocessing for footnotes/endnotes, styles and charts (src/document_comparer.rs:4685-4696,4724-4750,4861-4878), reached after admission and PartFs opening (6559-6568,6607-6625).

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> with_layout -> admit -> suffix-based XML check skips header.bin -> internal relationship resolution -> chrome_part_xml -> recursive parse_element -> stack exhaustion

impact.rationale: Host-process availability; no confidentiality, arbitrary file write or code-execution claim.

likelihood.rationale: Default parser path accepts the internally linked renamed payload; deep nesting is directly attacker-controlled.

reachability.summary: A document author needs only to have the consumer render the supplied package; no operator configuration change, filesystem access or network access is needed.
reachability.entrypoint: Public rendering and non-identical document-comparison paths
reachability.outcome: rendering process abort or equivalent stack exhaustion

attackPath.summary: Supply a DOCX with an ordinary main part, a section headerReference, an internal header relationship targeting header.bin, and a deeply nested well-formed XML payload at that target; render via the public PDF/PNG APIs or their wrappers.

remediationTests: An internal header/footer target named .bin with nesting above max_xml_depth must return INVALID_XML before DOM construction.
Repeat with custom part names and raised/lowered InputLimits; ordinary shallow parts must remain supported.
Repeat renamed-part admission regressions for styles, footnotes, endnotes and chart relationships in comparison preprocessing.

originalCandidates.message: Confirmed candidate: admission scans XML policy only when archive entry lower.ends_with('.xml'|'.rels') (src/admission.rs:534-545), special-cases only main_part missing extension (558-569). Renderer loads arbitrary header/footer relationship target without extension constraint (src/convert/mod.rs:20762-20779), passes directly to unbounded recursive Dom::parse_xdocument at 20794-20795; parse_element recursively invokes itself at src/xmllinq/parse.rs:660-662. An attacker can target word/header.bin and put deeply nested well-formed XML there, bypass max_xml_depth=256 and crash converter host via stack exhaustion. Investigating all entrypoint controls before final.

findings.title: Reading a small legacy DOC can expand repeated text pieces into billions of characters
findings.summary: A legacy DOC author can reuse the same physical WordDocument text range in many contiguous logical pieces. `main_text` expands every logical character into `StoryChar` without a decoded-character budget, exhausting host memory or CPU.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled parser input can deny availability through disproportionate work or allocation in default public paths. Impact is process availability with high likelihood for a crafted input; no remote exposure, confidentiality loss or code execution is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A disposable process with strict CPU/memory budgets reduces application-level impact; shared long-lived processing increases it.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source trace confirms the input-to-sink control gap and strongest counterevidence; no application or exploit execution was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Public legacy reader
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-supplied streams provide the FIB and piece table passed directly to main_text.

codeEvidence.label: Physical offsets and logical ranges
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker CP endpoints and fc offsets become pieces; separate pieces may retain the same physical offset.

codeEvidence.label: Coverage without expansion budget
codeEvidence.explanation: Increasing contiguous logical ranges pass without constraining their total decoded length.

codeEvidence.label: Expand every logical character
codeEvidence.explanation: Each logical CP derives an in-bounds physical offset and is decoded even when earlier pieces already referenced those bytes.

codeEvidence.label: Retain expanded characters
codeEvidence.explanation: The decoder pushes a new StoryChar for every logical character without an output budget.

codeEvidence.label: CLI routes OLE to converter
codeEvidence.explanation: OLE input reaches doc_to_docx before the later DOCX sniff/admission path.

rootCause.summary: `read` accepts the FIB main-story count and piece table, then passes them directly to `main_text`. Piece parsing permits each CP range to select the same physical fc range. The coverage check ensures contiguous increasing logical CPs but does not constrain their total decoded length relative to bytes or a resource limit. The per-character loop rereads the shared physical bytes and pushes a new StoryChar for every logical CP.

findings.remediation: Apply a configurable maximum decoded-character/output-byte budget before expansion and during emission; refuse excessive logical story length even when repeated physical ranges are individually valid.

counterEvidence: CFB sector-chain iteration is bounded by file size and invalid CP coverage is rejected.
No deployment exposure or measured allocation size is assumed; the exact StoryChar layout is platform dependent.
limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

dataflow.summary: legacy DOC bytes -> CompoundFile streams/FIB -> pieces -> main_text logical CP iteration -> StoryChar vector -> memory/CPU exhaustion

impact.rationale: CPU, memory or stack availability of the consuming process.

likelihood.rationale: The default source path accepts the required attacker-controlled representation without a bound on the demonstrated expansion.

reachability.summary: supplier of a legacy .doc consumed by legacy_doc::read, doc_to_markdown or doc_to_docx can trigger the affected public input path without changing trusted configuration.

findings.title: Opening duplicate relationship records performs quadratic repair work
findings.summary: A DOCX author can include many distinct relationship IDs, each repeated identically. The package loader retains these records for repair, and each duplicate scans the growing repaired-ID vector, causing quadratic CPU work within normal archive limits.

severity.rationale: Attacker-controlled parser input can deny availability through disproportionate work or allocation in default public paths. Impact is process availability with high likelihood for a crafted input; no remote exposure, confidentiality loss or code execution is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A disposable process with strict CPU/memory budgets reduces application-level impact; shared long-lived processing increases it.

confidence.rationale: Independent static source trace confirms the input-to-sink control gap and strongest counterevidence; no application or exploit execution was performed.

codeEvidence.label: Metadata retains all records
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker-controlled relationship list is retained for later duplicate repair.

codeEvidence.label: Every relationship set is repaired
codeEvidence.explanation: Opening the package runs duplicate repair on both package and part relationship sets.

codeEvidence.label: Linear scan for every new duplicate
codeEvidence.explanation: Identical duplicate IDs bypass conflicting-record refusal and scan every previously repaired ID.

rootCause.summary: `read_relationships` preserves the record list and `PartFs::open_within` invokes `drop_repeated_relationships`. Its `seen` map finds duplicates efficiently, but each duplicate then uses `repaired.contains` over all previously repaired IDs. Repeating each of N distinct IDs twice requires roughly N(N-1)/2 string comparisons.

findings.remediation: Track repaired IDs in a HashSet while retaining a Vec only for ordered output, and optionally bound total metadata records.

counterEvidence: Conflicting records under one ID are refused, but the attack uses identical pairs.
XML byte budgets bound input size, yet permit many records and do not bound quadratic work; process CPU limits can contain external impact.
limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: Metadata parsing preserves duplicate IDs (`rels.items = items`), and identical duplicates are intentionally repaired rather than rejected. A large shallow .rels fits XML depth/tag/byte caps and uses only one ZIP entry; max_entries limits ZIP members, not relationship records. No record-count bound precedes the vector scan.

dataflow.summary: attacker .rels records -> read_relationships items -> PartFs::open_within -> drop_repeated_relationships -> growing Vec::contains scan -> CPU exhaustion

impact.rationale: CPU, memory or stack availability of the consuming process.

codeEvidence.explanation: The numeric XML value becomes a colspan with a minimum only and no upper bound.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span` parses an attacker-controlled usize and only applies a minimum of one; row grid skips accept any positive usize. These counts become RawCell colspans. findings.remediation: Validate a practical total grid-column limit before accumulating or allocating, apply it to spans and skipped columns, and use checked arithmetic with typed refusal.

counterEvidence: Malformed/non-numeric attributes fall back safely; the exploit uses a valid numeric value.

limitations: Static-only validation; no runtime measurement or deployed embedding assessment.
validation.summary: A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.

findings.title: Tolerated XML syntax can hide recursive elements from admission
findings.summary: A DOCX author can place nested element text inside an XML comment after an unquoted attribute. Admission counts only shallow quick-xml events, while the permissive DOM parser consumes that attribute differently and recursively interprets the hidden tags. The normal .xml path can therefore exhaust the host stack despite max_xml_depth.

severity.rationale: A small crafted document can reliably cause disproportionate allocation or stack use in a public parser path; impact is process availability, likelihood high when consumed. No remote deployment is assumed.

confidence.rationale: Source establishes the complete relevant branch/control/dataflow. Runtime execution and deployment-specific exposure were not tested.

taxonomy.category: Parser interpretation conflict / XML depth bypass

codeEvidence.label: Admitted package reaches raw DOM
codeEvidence.explanation: The public conversion pipeline admits package bytes and later directly constructs the DOM.

codeEvidence.label: Admission counts one parser's events
codeEvidence.explanation: The gate uses tolerant attributes and counts only element events; comments and DocType do not contribute depth.

codeEvidence.label: Unquoted attributes intentionally accepted
codeEvidence.explanation: The package policy enables HTML-style unquoted/valueless attribute parsing.

codeEvidence.label: Raw parser consumes value as quoted
codeEvidence.explanation: An unquoted first value character becomes a delimiter and can carry parsing across a start tag into comment text.

codeEvidence.label: DOCTYPE skip stops too early
codeEvidence.explanation: The raw parser skips only to the first >, allowing internal-subset literal text to become later element input.

codeEvidence.label: Interpreted elements recurse
codeEvidence.explanation: Tags hidden from admission become recursive parse_element calls without an independent depth guard.

codeEvidence.label: Strict gate refuses DTD
codeEvidence.explanation: The checked XML API explicitly rejects DTD events; the tolerant package scan lacks this branch.

rootCause.summary: Admission uses quick-xml events and TagPolicy::tolerant, which accepts unquoted attributes, and ignores comments/DTD events for element depth. The downstream parser assumes the first attribute-value character is a quote delimiter even when it is not a quote. It can consume across the start-tag boundary into a comment, then parse comment content as real elements. Its DOCTYPE skip also stops at the first > rather than the end of an internal subset, creating a related interpretation gap.

findings.remediation: Make admission and DOM construction consume the same grammar, reject unsupported DTDs at package admission, parse unquoted values correctly or refuse them, and enforce a hard depth budget inside DOM construction.

counterEvidence: Correctly quoted ordinary XML without DTD/comment interpretation gaps receives the expected depth check.
Standalone checked XML parsing rejects the unquoted route and DTD; the report concerns public package processing using tolerant admission and raw DOM construction.
No external entity resolution, network/file access or entity expansion is claimed.
limitations: No application code or malicious fixture executed; platform/runtime behavior was assessed from source.
validation.summary: For the unquoted/comment route, `<r a=x><!-- x>` followed by nested tags and a comment close is a shallow root/comment sequence to admission; raw parse_element treats the first x as a quote and the x inside the comment as its close. It then reaches the nested tags without recognizing the comment opener it already consumed. No later depth guard exists before recursive parse_element. A DTD internal entity literal containing nested tags similarly falls under ignored DocType events but the raw skip consumes only the first >. These are grammar interpretation issues, not external-entity fetching. Strict validate_xml uses quoted attributes and explicitly refuses DTDs, but rendering's package-admission path does not invoke that strict gate.

dataflow.summary: DOCX .xml bytes -> check_xml_depth quick-xml/tolerant attribute policy -> shallow event depth -> raw parse_xdocument attribute/DOCTYPE interpretation -> hidden element recursion -> stack exhaustion

likelihood.rationale: Correctly quoted ordinary XML without DTD/comment interpretation gaps receives the expected depth check. Standalone checked XML parsing rejects the unquoted route and DTD; the report concerns public package processing using tolerant admission and raw DOM construction. No external entity resolution, network/file access or entity expansion is claimed.

rootCause.summary: The edit/add operation path calls _record after normal plan parsing and document preview. _record resolves the intended final plan but constructs a predictable sibling temporary path using the process ID. Path.write_bytes opens that path with normal truncate/follow semantics rather than exclusive creation or no-follow protection. os.replace happens only after the unintended referent has already been modified.

findings.remediation: Use the native staged publication helper or atomically create an unpredictable private temporary file with exclusive/no-follow semantics, retain its handle, then atomically replace the intended plan.

surfaces.label: Relationship-selected XML admission
surfaces.notes: Parent validated same suffix-based admission gap in renderer headers/footers and comparator style/note/chart relationship consumers; each source location is retained in the finding.

surfaces.label: Reading a small legacy DOC can expand repeated text pieces into billions of characters
surfaces.notes: Physical stream bounds, checked offset arithmetic and CFB chain limits prevent out-of-bounds reads and chain cycles, but do not limit logical text expansion. For example, 65,535 pieces each reusing a 64KiB compressed-text range describe about 4.29 billion decoded characters with under 1MiB of piece records. Every selected byte remains in bounds; the vector grows far beyond the input size. CLI legacy conversion routes OLE directly to doc_to_docx before DOCX admission.

surfaces.label: Opening duplicate relationship records performs quadratic repair work
surfaces.notes: Metadata parsing preserves duplicate IDs (`rels.items = items`), and identical duplicates are intentionally repaired rather than rejected. A large shallow .rels fits XML depth/tag/byte caps and uses only one ZIP entry; max_entries limits ZIP members, not relationship records. No record-count bound precedes the vector scan.

surfaces.label: Rendering a tiny table can allocate billions of columns
surfaces.riskArea: Unbounded allocation from numeric table metadata
surfaces.notes: A one-cell table with gridSpan=4294967295 requests approximately 16GiB for the f32 column vector on a 64-bit host. Larger accepted usize values can trigger capacity overflow. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows already occupying at least the declared grid and does not clamp them. `with_layout` admission bounds archive/XML bytes and structure, not these numeric counts.

surfaces.label: A cyclic Markdown drawing payload causes unbounded dependency recursion
surfaces.notes: A flat JSON graph containing one dependency with rel.part=0, reached by a top-level rel.part=0, passes index checks and immediately recurses on the same node forever. Serde's JSON nesting limit does not bound cycles represented as integer indices. `used` tracks output names, not visited dependency indices; late byte deduplication occurs only after recursive descent.

surfaces.label: Tolerated XML syntax can hide recursive elements from admission
surfaces.riskArea: Parser interpretation conflict / XML depth bypass
surfaces.notes: For the unquoted/comment route, `<r a=x><!-- x>` followed by nested tags and a comment close is a shallow root/comment sequence to admission; raw parse_element treats the first x as a quote and the x inside the comment as its close. It then reaches the nested tags without recognizing the comment opener it already consumed. No later depth guard exists before recursive parse_element. A DTD internal entity literal containing nested tags similarly falls under ignored DocType events but the raw skip consumes only the first >. These are grammar interpretation issues, not external-entity fetching. Strict validate_xml uses quoted attributes and explicitly refuses DTDs, but rendering's package-admission path does not invoke that strict gate.

surfaces.label: A large Chicago list or page number creates gigabytes of marker text
surfaces.notes: For n=4294967295, chicago_label computes i=4294967294 and repeats the three-byte double-dagger symbol 1073741824 times, requesting 3221225472 bytes before additional copies. A normal numbered paragraph with numFmt=chicago and lvlText=%1 reaches the list renderer. pgNumType/@start with fmt=chicago reaches the page-label branch, and Markdown list_marker delegates to list_number. ZIP/XML depth/byte bounds do not constrain the numeric expansion.
